findings:
🟠 [wdog-alive-scope-no-rp-no-fallback] MUST-FIX In `_watchdog_worker_alive`, the SCOPE_UNIT branch with `WORKER_RP` empty and `WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID` empty skips the `ps -o state=` probe entirely and falls to `_watchdog_pgid_has_live ""`, which returns 1 on the empty-target guard before ever consulting ps. The watchdog therefore exits at the deadline without stamping `.fired` or invoking `systemctl --user kill`, even though the scope kill needs no pgid and would work. This is exactly the "SCOPE_UNIT with WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID empty + WORKER_RP empty" shape the spec obligation names as a finding, and it fails closed in the wrong direction (unknown treated as dead). Reachability today is narrow: `_wait_worker_with_watchdog` assigns `WORKER_RP="$rp"` before arming, so run_worker never hits it; it only bites a caller arming the watchdog directly. Smallest fix: in the SCOPE_UNIT branch, `if [ -z "$rp" ] && [ -z "${WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID:-}" ]; then return 0; fi` before the fallback pgid check, and add that shape (rp unset, fallback unset, ps stubbed to exit 1, expect rc 0) to `assert_r7_scope_unknown_state_no_fallback_fires`. The plain-branch analogue (WORKER_SID and fallback both empty → dead) is not a defect because `_watchdog_signal_worker` has no target there either, so firing is impossible.
🔵 [test-reap-pid-dead-recycle] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `assert_r8_detached_reaps_worker_session_descendants` calls `reap_pid "$sleeper"` / `reap_pid "$sleeperi"` after `wait_pid_dead` has already confirmed the pid dead, so the bare `kill -KILL` targets a pid the test knows is gone; under pid wraparound it could hit an unrelated process. No pkill/pgrep pattern in the new test file matches broadly and every other `reap_pid` call is on a live `$!` child or a still-alive stub, so this is the only spot. Excluded now: needs a full pid wrap within seconds; fix by skipping `reap_pid` when `wait_pid_dead` returned 0.
🔵 [test-env-knobs-in-prod] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `HETERO_TEST_SYSTEMCTL_KILL_FAIL`, `HETERO_TEST_NO_SETSID` and `HETERO_TEST_NO_JOBCONTROL` are honoured unconditionally by the production script; an inherited `HETERO_TEST_SYSTEMCTL_KILL_FAIL=1` silently downgrades the cgroup kill to the pgid fallback. Excluded: the dispatcher already trusts its caller-supplied env and no rail sets these; consider gating them behind a single test-mode switch later.
🔵 [nosetsid-untagged-sleeper-cancel] CUT/FOLLOW-UP On the no-setsid fallback the watchdog sleeper is a plain `sleep "$secs"` with no `hetero-wall-watchdog-<tag>` in its cmdline, so the new `_watchdog_sleeppid_cmdline_has_tag` gate means `_cancel_worker_watchdog` never kills it directly and the tag-scoped pkill cannot reach it either; it relies solely on the subshell TERM trap `kill "${sp:-}"`. If the subshell is gone the untagged sleep lingers for the remaining timeout but cannot fire (token already removed). Excluded: harmless leak, no-setsid hosts only; could `exec -a` the fallback sleeper too.
